questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explain: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is the biggest?
questions.explain: Jupiter is so big that all the other planets would fit inside it.

questions.q: Which planet is the smallest?
questions.explain: Mercury is only a bit bigger than our Moon.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune is about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth.

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explain: Earth is our home, the third planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is called the red planet?
questions.explain: Mars looks red because its dust and rocks contain rust.

questions.q: Which planet has the biggest, brightest rings?
questions.explain: Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest?
questions.explain: Venus is wrapped in thick clouds that trap heat, so it is hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: Which planet is the second from the Sun?
questions.explain: Venus comes after Mercury.

questions.q: Which planet is the fourth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Mars comes right after Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is a giant covered in stripes?
questions.explain: Jupiter's stripes are clouds of gas pulled into bands by its fast spin.

questions.q: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
questions.explain: The Great Red Spot has been swirling for hundreds of years.

questions.q: Which planet is deep blue and has the fastest winds?
questions.explain: Neptune's winds are faster than a jet plane.

questions.q: Which planet has the tallest volcano, Olympus Mons?
questions.explain: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.

questions.q: Which planet is between Mars and Saturn?
questions.explain: The order goes Mars, Jupiter, Saturn.

questions.q: On which planet would you feel the heaviest?
questions.explain: Jupiter pulls hardest on you: about 2.5 times as much as Earth.

questions.q: Which planet spins on its side, like a rolling ball?
questions.explain: Something big may have knocked Uranus over long ago.

questions.q: Which planet is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub?
questions.explain: Saturn is mostly gas, so it is lighter than water for its size.

questions.q: Which planet is nearly the same size as Earth and is called Earth's twin?
questions.explain: Venus is almost as wide as Earth, but it is a very hot place.

questions.q: Which planet is the seventh from the Sun?
questions.explain: Uranus comes after Saturn and before Neptune.

questions.q: Which planet is the sixth from the Sun?
questions.explain: Saturn comes after Jupiter.

questions.q: Pluto is no longer called a planet. What is it called now?
questions.explain: Pluto is round like a planet but smaller than our Moon, so in 2006 scientists called it a dwarf planet.

questions.q: How many planets are there in our solar system?
questions.explain: There are eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune.

questions.q: Which planet takes the longest to go once around the Sun?
questions.explain: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years for one trip.

questions.q: Which planet spins so fast that its day is shorter than 10 hours?
questions.explain: A day on Jupiter lasts only about 10 hours, even though it is huge.

questions.q: Which planet is the only one not named after a god?
questions.explain: The other seven planets are named after Roman or Greek gods.

questions.q: Which planet looks the brightest in our night sky?
questions.explain: Venus reflects lots of sunlight from its clouds and comes close to Earth.

questions.q: Which is the biggest of the four rocky planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars)?
questions.explain: Earth is a little bigger than Venus.

questions.q: On which planet would you feel about 2.5 times heavier than on Earth?
questions.explain: Jupiter's gravity is 2.53 times Earth's.

questions.q: Mars pulls you with 0.38 times Earth's gravity. How heavy would you feel on Mars?
questions.explain: 0.38 is a bit more than one-third, so you would feel much lighter. Mercury pulls just the same!

questions.q: Which of these planets is NOT a giant made of gas or ice?
questions.explain: Mars is a small rocky planet; Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, Neptune an ice giant.
